note: Movement library. Stable across program revisions — program.json references these by id.

exercises.name: Seated hip flexor isometric, mid-range
exercises.setup: Sit on a chair, knee at 90 degrees.
cues: Press the thigh up into your own hands at about 60 percent effort
Keep breathing throughout the hold
Loads the flexors in the range that does not provoke you
exercises.avoid: This is NOT a straight-leg raise and NOT a hanging movement.
exercises.video_search: seated hip flexor isometric hold rehab

exercises.name: Long-lever hip flexor isometric
exercises.setup: Supine, leg extended to roughly 30 degrees of hip flexion, hold against a band or partner resistance.
cues: Longer lever means more load — only progress here once the seated version is easy and symptom-free

exercises.name: Standing banded march
cues: Knee to roughly 90 degrees only
Controlled lowering — the lowering phase is where clicking was documented

exercises.name: Adductor isometric squeeze, knees bent
exercises.setup: Supine, ball or rolled towel between the knees, knees bent to 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Adductor isometric squeeze, knees at 45 degrees
cues: Longer lever, more load

exercises.name: Copenhagen plank, short lever
cues: Knee on the bench, not the ankle
Long-lever version is a later goal, not a starting point

exercises.name: Glute bridge
cues: Ribs down
Do not arch the lower back to finish the rep — finish with the glute

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
cues: Left side first, one extra set on the left — documented left gluteus maximus deficit

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
cues: Chin tucked
Ribs down
Finish with the glute, not the lower back
exercises.rationale: Best heavy glute-max builder with essentially zero spinal shear and no lumbar extension moment. The anchor lift — progress it aggressively.

exercises.name: Dead bug, slow
cues: Lower back stays flat against the floor throughout
If it lifts, shorten the range
exercises.rationale: Anti-extension trunk work — the single most relevant home exercise for the Bertolotti segment.

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.rationale: The transitional segment dislikes rotation under load. Builds tolerance for it.

exercises.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
cues: Dumbbells at your sides, or front-racked
Front foot far enough forward that the shin stays fairly vertical
Knee tracks over the toe — knee caving inward is FADIR under load
exercises.video_search: rear foot elevated split squat setup

exercises.name: Heavy sled push or drag
exercises.rationale: Near-zero spinal load, high leg force, transfers directly to running mechanics. If you only did hip thrusts and heavy sled you would still get most of the result.

exercises.name: Nordic curl (or GHR, or slider leg curl)
exercises.rationale: Posterior chain strength with no spinal load at all.

exercises.name: Front squat
cues: More upright torso, smaller lumbar extension moment than back squat
Knees out
Use lifting straps in the rack if the standard front-rack aggravates the right shoulder

exercises.name: High-bar back squat
cues: Bar sits on the traps, not the rear delts — low-bar rack position is OFF the menu due to shoulder retroversion
Upright torso, knees out, controlled descent
If the grip aggravates the right shoulder, take a wider grip or use lifting straps around the bar
exercises.rationale: Primary working squat variant. High-bar produces a more vertical torso than low-bar and a smaller lumbar extension moment — safer over a Bertolotti segment. It's also the version this user can rack given the posterior shoulder pathology.

exercises.name: Safety squat bar back squat
cues: SSB handles in front — no shoulder external rotation required to rack the bar
The camber pushes you forward, so brace hard and stay upright
exercises.rationale: The friendliest heavy squat variant for this shoulder. If the box has one, prefer SSB for the main squat slot until the shoulder is a solved problem.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat, dumbbells
cues: Dumbbells at your sides
Front shin close to vertical — knee-forward drive loads the labrum
Left side gets the extra set — documented left glute-max and left hip-flexor deficit
exercises.rationale: Heavier progression of the RFE split squat. Unilateral loading is the primary tool for closing the left-right strength gap the record documents.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
cues: Kettlebell or dumbbell in the opposite hand to the working leg
Hinge at the hip, keep the spine long, do not round the low back
Left side gets the extra set
exercises.rationale: Unilateral posterior-chain loading, teaches hip hinge with a stable spine, and closes the left glute-max gap. Non-negotiable in every training week.

exercises.name: Block pull, mid-shin height

default.setup_note: bar starts at mid-shin, ~10-15 cm elevated

cues: Shortens the range of motion, reduces the flexion demand at the pull start
Neutral spine, brace before you lift, drive with the legs
This is the primary heavy pull until conventional deadlift is symptom-free

exercises.name: Conventional deadlift from the floor
cues: Only if the block pull has been symptom-free at ~150 kg for at least 4 weeks
Brace hard, neutral spine, lats engaged, drive the floor away
Any left SI or groin symptom in the next-morning check means back to block pulls

exercises.name: Daily air-squat skill practice
cues: Bodyweight or empty bar only
Slow tempo, full depth without pain, focus on knees tracking over toes
This is technique work and joint nutrition, NOT stimulus — do not chase fatigue
exercises.rationale: Frequency practice. The research signal on daily squatting is that it produces better technique and consistency, not more hypertrophy. Treat it as skill practice.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Dumbbell or kettlebell held at the chest
Full depth without knees caving

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
cues: Heavy weight in one hand only
Stay tall, ribs down, do not lean toward the load
exercises.rationale: Anti-lateral-flexion + anti-rotation loaded carry — direct fit for the left transitional segment.

exercises.name: Farmer's carry
cues: Heavy weight in both hands
Tall posture, controlled breathing, small fast steps

exercises.name: Trap-bar deadlift from blocks
cues: Neutral grip, less shear than a straight bar

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
cues: Posterior pelvic tilt FIRST
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg
Only lean until you feel a mild stretch
exercises.warning: You should feel it in the front of the thigh, not deep in the groin or the front of the hip joint. Deep anterior hip pinching means you are loading the labrum — back off immediately.
exercises.video_search: half kneeling hip flexor stretch posterior pelvic tilt

exercises.name: 90/90 hip switches
cues: Controlled, no bouncing
Stay inside the pain-free range
Skip if it pinches

exercises.name: A-march
cues: Knee to approximately 90 degrees only

exercises.name: Controlled leg swings, front to back
cues: Small range — this is a primer, not a stretch

exercises.name: Hollow hold
exercises.notes: Substitute for GHD sit-ups and kipping toes-to-bar in class.

exercises.name: Strict knee raise to 90 degrees
cues: Stop at 90 degrees
Slow, controlled lowering
exercises.notes: Substitute for kipping toes-to-bar. Watch the shoulder as well as the hip.

exercises.name: Zone 1/2 steady-state cardio (row / bike / ski-erg / run)
exercises.setup: Pick your intake modality. Warm up 5 min at very easy effort, then hold the target zone for the prescribed duration. Cool down 3-5 min.
cues: Nose-breathing pace, or 'you could hold a conversation in full sentences'
Heart rate 60-70% max, RPE 3-4/10
Cadence steady, form clean — this is not a slog to grind out
exercises.rationale: Zone 1/2 steady-state builds mitochondrial density, capillary networks, and fat oxidation. It is the largest single driver of aerobic capacity across the whole 3-block arc. Boring and non-negotiable.
exercises.notes: If you finish and want to keep going, you were probably at the right effort. If you finish gassed, you went too hard.

exercises.name: Sustained tempo (row / bike / ski-erg / run)
exercises.setup: Warm up 10-12 min including 2 x 30s pickups. Then hold a comfortably hard, sustainable pace for the prescribed block. Cool down 5 min.
cues: 83-88% of VDOT pace / 88-94% of FTP / 82-87% HRmax
'Comfortably hard' — you could talk in short sentences, not full paragraphs
If you can't finish the block at the same pace you started, back off next time
exercises.rationale: Sub-threshold sustained work drives mitochondrial biogenesis and lifts the lactate curve without generating the fatigue cost of true threshold intervals. Sits between Z2 and Norwegian 4x4 in the arc.
exercises.video_search: tempo run sweetspot cycling how to

exercises.name: Threshold cruise intervals (row / bike / ski-erg / run)
exercises.setup: Warm up 12-15 min including 3 x 30s pickups. Hold threshold pace on each interval; walk / very easy spin between. Cool down 5-8 min.
cues: 85-90% HRmax, RPE 7/10
The pace you could hold for a hard hour
Even splits across sets — if set 3 is 10s slower than set 1, you started too hot
exercises.rationale: Longer sub-VO2max intervals raise lactate clearance capacity and central cardiac output without the recovery hit of 4x4. Complements the Norwegian block by widening the sub-threshold plateau.

exercises.name: Norwegian 4x4 intervals (row / bike / ski-erg / run)
exercises.setup: Warm up 12-15 min including 3 x 30s pickups. 4 x 4 minutes at 90-95% HRmax with 3 minutes of active recovery (very easy) between. Cool down 8-10 min.
cues: First minute is a lie — pace should feel comfortable, then progressively hurt
By interval 3-4, HR should sit in the top window from about minute 2 onwards
Active recovery is easy pedal / stride / stroke, not a full stop
exercises.rationale: The single best-studied VO2max protocol (Helgerud 2007). Time-in-zone at 90-95% HRmax drives stroke volume adaptation faster than any other interval structure of comparable duration.
exercises.notes: This session costs more recovery than any other in Block 1. Never place it within 48 h of another hard session. If HR won't come up on set 1, you're too tired — swap to Z1 and try again in 48 h.

exercises.name: Easy recovery spin / row / walk-jog
exercises.setup: Very easy effort on your chosen modality. Purpose is blood flow and recovery, not adaptation.
cues: Nose-breathing throughout
HR under 65% max
If it feels like a workout, back off
exercises.rationale: Recovery sessions accelerate lactate clearance and glycogen replenishment vs total rest, without adding fatigue cost. Sits in the same category as the daily home block for legs — protective, not productive.

exercises.name: Engine retest session
exercises.setup: Repeat whichever benchmarks you set at intake. In order: (1) resting HR — take before getting out of bed; (2) 5-min submax HR at the same easy pace you used at intake; (3) 500m row TT if you rowed at intake; (4) 1km run TT if you ran at intake. Space TTs by at least 15 min of easy spin.
cues: Same modality, same equipment, same time of day if you can
Not every metric will apply — record what you can do
Rest HR + submax HR at fixed pace are always measurable and the most sensitive early indicators
exercises.rationale: Same protocol at start and end so the delta means something. Rest HR drop and submax HR drop at the same pace are the two cleanest indicators of aerobic adaptation in 8 weeks.

exercises.name: Wrist extension prep on floor
exercises.setup: Kneel with palms flat on the floor, fingers spread, fingertips pointing toward knees. Gently rock weight forward onto the heels of the hands, then rotate to fingertips-out, then fingertips-in. 5 slow reps per direction.
cues_external_focus: Rock your weight over the floor like you're smoothing wet sand
Spread the fingers so each knuckle takes an even share of the floor

exercises.name: Wrist push-ups on floor
exercises.setup: Kneel, place backs of the hands on the floor with palms up, then push off the floor onto knuckles or palms. Slow tempo, 3s down, 1s up.
cues_external_focus: Push the floor away smoothly, like closing a heavy drawer
Land quietly on the backs of the hands — no slap

exercises.name: Finger raises (planche prep)
exercises.setup: On all fours or in a plank, press hands flat then lift the fingers off the floor one at a time (thumb → pinky) and back. Keep palm pressure through the heel of the hand.
cues_external_focus: Peel each finger off the floor like it's stuck to paper
Keep the whole palm heel pressing down as you lift

exercises.name: Fingertip taps against wall
exercises.setup: Stand facing a wall, arms extended, fingertips lightly on the wall. Tap fingers rhythmically on the wall while holding a soft plank shape through the torso.
cues_external_focus: Drum the wall like a piano — light, even, no thump
Hold your ribs stacked over your hips as if a book balanced on your chest

exercises.name: Hollow body hold
exercises.setup: Supine, low back pressed to the floor, arms overhead, legs straight and low. Hold the shape without letting the low back arch up.
cues_external_focus: Press the small of your back into the floor like you're pinning a card there
Aim fingertips at one wall and toes at the opposite wall — long line

exercises.name: Hollow body rock
exercises.setup: From a hollow hold, rock forward and back along the length of the spine without breaking the shape.
cues_external_focus: Rock the whole shape like a rocking chair — no wobble in the middle
Keep the low back glued to the floor at the bottom of every rock

exercises.name: Arch hold (superman)
exercises.setup: Prone, arms overhead, lift chest and legs off the floor, hold. Balances the hollow-body shape with posterior-chain engagement.
cues_external_focus: Reach fingertips and toes toward opposite walls
Lift the ribs off the floor as if a string is pulling your sternum up

exercises.name: Kinoshita position 1 — 90 degree incline hold
exercises.setup: Hands on the floor, feet elevated on a low box or step so the hip is at roughly 90 degrees flexion. Support the inverted upper body with straight arms. Small easy dose while shoulder overhead endurance is built.
cues_external_focus: Push the floor away so your shoulders sit high above the hands
Look at a spot on the floor between your hands, not forward

exercises.name: Kinoshita position 2 — 135 degree incline hold
exercises.setup: Hands on the floor, feet elevated higher (e.g. bench, plyo box) so hip angle opens to roughly 135 degrees. Straighter line, more shoulder overhead demand than the 90 position.
cues_external_focus: Drive the box away from your hands, not your hands away from the box
Point the crown of your head at the wall opposite you

exercises.name: Kinoshita position 3 — elbow stand / straddle L stand
exercises.setup: From the floor, invert into a straddle-L stand (legs wide, hips over hands) or an elbow stand. Both develop the near-vertical shoulder position without full overhead demand.
cues_external_focus: Push the floor down toward China — long arms, high shoulders
Spread your feet toward opposite corners of the ceiling

exercises.name: Wall walk
exercises.setup: Start prone with feet against a wall. Walk feet up the wall while walking hands closer to the wall until chest is near the wall. Reverse to return.
cues_external_focus: Walk your hands toward the wall, not your feet up the wall
Point your toes at the ceiling at the top

exercises.name: Wall handstand hold — chest to wall
exercises.setup: Kick or wall-walk into a handstand facing the wall (chest and thighs lightly on wall). Hold the plumb-line shape.
cues_external_focus: Push the floor away — imagine growing an inch taller against the wall
Point toes at the ceiling and squeeze a coin between the heels

exercises.name: Wall handstand hold — belly to wall (kick-up)
exercises.setup: Kick up to a handstand back-to-wall, heels lightly touching wall. Wrist strategy dominates balance here (Kerwin & Trewartha 2001) — press fingers or heels of palms to adjust.
cues_external_focus: Press fingertips into the floor when you feel the toes drift away from the wall
Point toes to the ceiling — long line from wrists to heels
exercises.video_search: back to wall handstand kick up hold

exercises.name: Wall-supported handstand shrugs
exercises.setup: Chest-to-wall handstand. Shrug shoulders up (protract / elevate) then let them settle. Slow tempo. Builds serratus + trap endurance in the overhead position.
cues_external_focus: Push the floor away hard, then let it come 2cm closer, then push again
Grow tall each rep as if reaching for a shelf above

exercises.name: Wall handstand shoulder taps
exercises.setup: Chest-to-wall handstand. Slowly shift weight onto one hand and tap the opposite shoulder with the free hand. Alternate.
cues_external_focus: Shift over the loaded hand as slowly as pouring honey
Tap and place softly — no rush back to the floor

exercises.name: Freestanding kick-up practice
exercises.setup: Away from any wall. Kick up to what should be a handstand and try to hold the top for a beat before coming down. Use a spotter or a soft floor. Focus on kicking to balance, not past it.
cues_external_focus: Aim the kick to reach the top and stop, not fly past
Send the crown of your head toward the wall in front of you as you kick

exercises.name: Freestanding hold attempt
exercises.setup: Kick up and try to hold freestanding as long as possible. Log seconds each attempt.
cues_external_focus: Fingertips press small circles on the floor to steer
Aim toes at one fixed spot on the ceiling

exercises.name: Tuck freestand hold
exercises.setup: Freestanding with knees tucked to chest. Reduces the moment of inertia so balance is easier — a bridging step for early freestanders.
cues_external_focus: Squeeze knees to chest like hugging a ball
Press fingertips into the floor to hunt the balance point

exercises.name: Single-step walk attempts
exercises.setup: Freestand and deliberately shift weight onto one hand, take one step, replace the other. Even one clean step counts as a rep.
cues_external_focus: Lean the shape toward the far wall so the step happens on its own
Land the moving hand quietly, no slap

exercises.name: 2-3 step shuttle walks
exercises.setup: Freestand, walk 2-3 steps, come down, reset. Repeat. Short shuttles beat one long attempt (Shea & Morgan 1979 CI + spacing).
cues_external_focus: Send the shape toward the far end of the room
Break the walk into small quiet steps, not big lunges

exercises.name: Continuous walk along a line
exercises.setup: Mark a straight line on the floor with tape. Kick up and walk as far as possible along the line before coming down. Log distance.
cues_external_focus: Track the line with your eyes as it passes between your hands
Lean the shape toward the far end and let steps chase

exercises.name: Walking between markers (path variability)
exercises.setup: Place small markers (chalk / floor stickers) 1-2 hand-widths apart along a path. Walk hand-over-hand landing each hand near a marker. Trains contact placement precision.
cues_external_focus: Land each hand next to its marker like stepping stones
Follow the trail of markers with your eyes

exercises.name: Half pirouette on wall (180 turn)
exercises.setup: Chest-to-wall handstand. Walk hands around 180 degrees to end back-to-wall (or vice versa). Slow, controlled — this is the turn pattern in half-scale.
cues_external_focus: Walk your hands around the clock face slowly — one o'clock, two o'clock
Keep the crown of your head over the same tile the whole turn

exercises.name: Half pirouette freestanding (180 turn)
exercises.setup: From a freestanding handstand, turn 180 degrees on the hands and continue. Advanced skill — attempt with a spotter or over a soft mat.
cues_external_focus: Look for the wall behind you as if turning to check traffic
Push one hand into the floor to swing the shape around

exercises.name: Full pirouette freestanding (360 turn)
exercises.setup: From a freestanding handstand walk, execute a full 360-degree turn and continue walking. Elite-level skill.
cues_external_focus: Spot the same wall twice on the way round
Let each hand-plant power the next arc of the turn

exercises.name: Walking over a 5kg plate
exercises.setup: Place a 5kg (or bumper) plate on the floor mid-path. Handstand walk toward and over it, placing one hand past the plate at a time.
cues_external_focus: See the plate arrive between your hands and step past it
Land the far hand past the plate before lifting the near hand

exercises.name: Walking through cones (path variability)
exercises.setup: Space small cones or blocks along a serpentine path. Walk on hands through the pattern, weaving as required.
cues_external_focus: Weave your shape between the cones like a skier
Look ahead at the next cone, not down at the one you're at

exercises.name: Precision path (narrow-lane walking)
exercises.setup: Mark a narrow lane (2 parallel tape lines about a shoulder-width apart). Walk the full length without crossing the lines. Precision constraint sharpens balance control.
cues_external_focus: Track the two tape lines like train tracks running under you
Land each hand between the lines — quiet and precise

exercises.name: Downward-dog wrist recovery
exercises.setup: After session, hold a downward-dog / pike position with soft knees. Shift weight side to side across the palms. Aim for a 30-60 second decompression.
cues_external_focus: Rock the palms side to side as if wringing out a towel
Send the sternum toward the thighs

exercises.name: Child's pose + wrist stretches
exercises.setup: Kneel back into child's pose. From here perform the reverse-hand + palm-out wrist stretches for 20-30s each direction.
cues_external_focus: Melt the chest toward the floor
Send fingertips toward opposite walls in each stretch

exercises.name: Video review of last set
exercises.setup: Optional self-selected feedback: record one attempt and re-watch it once before the next set. Do NOT re-watch every attempt. Self-controlled schedule outperforms forced schedules (Chiviacowsky & Wulf 2002).
cues_external_focus: Watch the shape against the vertical line of the wall in the clip
Pick one thing to change on the next attempt — no more

class_modifications.reason: End-range lumbar extension over a pseudoarthrosis with bone oedema. Worst single movement on the list.
Doubles up: hanging loaded hip flexion (documented provocateur, with clicking) plus a hanging shoulder with a SLAP and posterior labral detachment.
Shoulder — SLAP plus posterior labrum plus spinoglenoid ganglion cyst.

class_modifications.avoid: Heavy back squat or deadlift for time
class_modifications.reason: Fatigue plus load plus lumbar flexion-extension cycling.
Lumbar extension plus overhead shoulder demand.
substitute: hang power snatch at moderate load

class_modifications.reason: Knees caving equals flexion plus adduction plus internal rotation under load — the positive test position.
class_modifications.action: Cue knees out, reduce depth when form degrades
